findings.title: website_name leaks the website for TL0 users hidden from anonymous viewers
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous guardian, `include_website?` returns false and the website is hidden. The new `website_name` attribute is not covered: `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` and never calls `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. As a result the website host, and now the full path, is still serialized for those users, bypassing the trust-level restriction. Gate `include_website_name` the same way as the untrusted attributes, and add `website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` expectation in the spec.

findings.title: Trailing slash appended when the website URL has only a root path
findings.body: For a website such as `http://example.com/`, `URI(...).path` is `/`, so `website_name` becomes `example.com/` when the discourse host matches. The path logic is also repeated in three branches, so this edge case is duplicated and easy to miss. Normalize the path (e.g. treat `/` as empty) before concatenating.

findings.title: Path-display branches are only partially covered by tests
findings.body: The spec covers the same-host case, the parent-domain case, and the unrelated-domain case. It does not cover the www/forum sibling branch (same depth, shared parent), a website with no path, or a website with a trailing slash. Each of these exercises a distinct branch of `website_name`, and the trailing-slash case currently produces an incorrect result.
